record.original_question: For the degree-2n polynomial p_{2n} with weight w(x) = x^gamma (1 - x)^alpha (1 + x)^beta, where alpha, beta, gamma > -1 and p_{2n} has exactly n zeros in each of the intervals (-1, 0) and (0, 1), does there exist an electrostatic model in which each set of n zeros is an equilibrium configuration of positive unit charges subject to mutual logarithmic repulsion, fixed charges alpha/2, beta/2, gamma/2 at 1, -1, 0, and n charges of weight 1/2 placed on the opposite subinterval?

evidence.quote: It is a real case: p2n has exactly n zeros in each interval (-1, 0) and (0, 1).

The asymptotic analysis (using the tools of the potential theory) suggests that a reasonable model for these zeros might be that each of these sets of n zeros is the equilibrium position of the positive unit charges, which besides the mutual interaction are subject to the external field generated by the three fixed charges alpha/2, beta/2, gamma/2 at 1, -1, 0, respectively, and by the n charges of the weight 1/2 on the other subinterval. Nevertheless, this is an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma>-1$ and consider the weight $w(x)=|x|^{\gamma}(1-x)^{\alpha}(1+x)^{\beta}$ on $[-1,1]$. For each positive integer $n$, let $p_{2n}$ denote the monic polynomial of degree $2n$ characterized by the multiple orthogonality conditions
$$\int_{-1}^{0} p_{2n}(x)\,x^{k}\,w(x)\,dx = 0, \qquad \int_{0}^{1} p_{2n}(x)\,x^{k}\,w(x)\,dx = 0, \qquad k=0,1,\dots,n-1.$$
Assume the real case in which $p_{2n}$ has exactly $n$ simple zeros in $(-1,0)$ and exactly $n$ simple zeros in $(0,1)$; denote these zero sets by $X^{-}=\{x_1^{-},\dots,x_n^{-}\}\subset(-1,0)$ and $X^{+}=\{x_1^{+},\dots,x_n^{+}\}\subset(0,1)$.

Consider the following electrostatic model. Place fixed external charges $\alpha/2$ at $1$, $\beta/2$ at $-1$, and $\gamma/2$ at $0$, and assume all free charges interact via the planar logarithmic potential ($U(z,w)=-\log|z-w|$). Place $n$ free positive unit charges $y_1,\dots,y_n\in(0,1)$ and $n$ free positive unit charges $z_1,\dots,z_n\in(-1,0)$. Additionally, regard each unit charge in one subinterval as exerting an attenuated influence on the other subinterval: from the perspective of the charges in $(0,1)$, each of the $n$ charges in $(-1,0)$ contributes with weight $1/2$, and symmetrically for the charges in $(-1,0)$.

Determine whether there exists a precise formulation of this two-component electrostatic problem under which the equilibrium configuration of the two systems of $n$ unit charges (minimizing the corresponding total energy on $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1)$) coincides with the zero sets $X^{-}$ and $X^{+}$ of $p_{2n}$ for every $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of giving an electrostatic interpretation of the zeros of Jacobi-Angelesco-type multiple orthogonal polynomials on two touching intervals was explicitly stated as open. Subsequent work on electrostatic models for zeros of multiple orthogonal polynomials (e.g., the "Electrostatic partners" approach of Martínez-Finkelshtein and Rakhmanov, 2022) develops vector-equilibrium interpretations for Angelesco-type systems, but no source found explicitly confirms a resolution of the specific charge-model conjecture (with fixed charges α/2, β/2, γ/2 at 1, -1, 0 and weight-1/2 mirror charges on the opposite subinterval) for this Jacobi-Angelesco family. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic partners and zeros of orthogonal and multiple orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: develops an electrostatic interpretation of zeros of type II multiple orthogonal polynomials in terms of a vector equilibrium, with more detailed results in Angelesco, Nikishin and generalized Nikishin cases
status_evidence.claim: Provides general electrostatic interpretations via vector equilibrium but does not explicitly settle the specific Jacobi-Angelesco two-interval model with the stated charges.

status_evidence.title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: Old, new, and some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems regarding electrostatic models for zeros of orthogonal and multiple orthogonal polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The electrostatic-model question for multiple orthogonal polynomials on touching intervals is listed among open problems.
